To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the band gap and effective masses of silicon nanowire are highly sensitive to strain.

(1) the conduction band edge has almost no variation, the second conduction band valley located at 1/3 pi/a of the Brilluoin zone moves down in energy, the top valence band shifts up in energy with tensile and compressional strain.

the band gap of silicon nanowire is reduced by 7%, and the effective mass of electrons and holes are increased by 10% and 20% respectively, when 2% compressive or tensile strain is applied to the silicon nanowires.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of uniaxinial strain on the electronic structure of silicon nanowire.
the study of bandstructures of Si nanowires of various diameters under the application of tensile and compressile strain.
the study of the effects of uniaaxial strain on the electronic properties of silicon nanowire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

strain can be used as an effective tool for tuning the band gap of nanowire transistors, which can be used for tuning the threshold voltage and the sub threshold swing of nanowire field effect transistors.
strain can be effectively used to tune the band structures of silicon nanowire based devices.
the band gap of silicon nanowire is highly sensitive to uniaxial strains, and the electron and hole effective masses show different dependence on strain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the band gap and the effective mass of the holes are the most sensitive to strain among the parameters studied.

the conduction band edge is almost strain insensitive, the second valley moves down in energy and the band gap reduces significantly with strain, and the effective masses show opposite dependence on the strain.
the strain has almost no effect on the conduction band edge but has a significant effect on the valence band edge and therefore the band gap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strain has significant effects on the electronic properties of silicon nanowire and can therefore be exploited for designing novel electronic devices.
the strain effects on the bandstructures are significant and should be considered in the design of nanowire-based nanoelectronics.
the band structure and effective masses are sensitive to the strain and hence, the strain effects should be taken into account while designing the devices based on nanowires.
